sections.history: Thiruthevanarthogai lies in the hamlet of Keezhchalai beside Thirunangur, near Sirkazhi, in Chola Nadu, and is also called the Madhava Perumal temple after its festival image. It is one of the 108 Divya Desams sung by the Alvars in the Nalayira Divya Prabandham, and one of the eleven Thirunangur Tirupathis hymned by Thirumangai Alvar. The presiding Lord is Deivanayaka Perumal, standing and facing east, with the Goddess Kadalmagal Nachiyar; the utsavars are Madhava Perumal and Madhava Nayaki. No inscription or royal patron is firmly recorded, so its age rests on the Alvar's hymns, placed between the seventh and ninth centuries.
sections.architecture: A fairly small Dravidian temple, entered through a three-tiered gopuram. The vimana over the sanctum is of the Sopana type. Within, Deivanayaka Perumal stands facing east, with Kadalmagal Nachiyar as his consort, while the processional images of Madhava Perumal and Madhava Nayaki are the forms taken out on festival days. Its modest scale suits the quiet hamlet around it and the unhurried pace of a village pilgrimage.
sections.legends: The name Devanar Thogai means the gathering of the devas. Tradition connects it with the Goddess, who is called Kadalmagal, the daughter of the ocean, because she is held to have been born of the sea; all the devas, the story says, were present at the churning of the ocean, and so the place is remembered as their assembly. The Lord here is thus Deivanayakan, the chief of the gods, standing among them.
sections.festivals: The temple joins the Garuda Sevai on the day after Thai Amavasai (January–February), when its utsavar, Madhava Perumal, is taken on a Garuda vahana to Thirumanimadam to meet the other lords of Thirunangur. The Thirumangai Alvar Mangalasasana Utsavam recalls the hymns. Tradition holds that seeing all eleven together equals visiting each one.
sections.experience: A small hamlet shrine that rewards a slow visit: stand before the east-facing Lord, then ask to see the festival images of Madhava Perumal and his consort. Keezhchalai lies close to Thirunangur, about 10 km by road from Sirkazhi, and is easily combined with the other Tirupathis in a day.

visit.timings: Darshan is generally held in morning and evening sessions with a midday break; the Garuda Sevai day is by far the busiest. Confirm timings locally before visiting.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional dress is expected — shoulders and knees covered; footwear removed before entering. Follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.photography: Photography is restricted in and around the sanctum; follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.gettingThere: Thirunangur lies about 10 km by road south-east of Sirkazhi (Sirkali) in Mayiladuthurai district. Sirkazhi, on the Chennai–Mayiladuthurai railway line, is the nearest station, and Tiruchirappalli, about 160 km away, the nearest major airport. Auto-rickshaws and taxis from Sirkazhi reach the village; the eleven shrines lie among paddy fields close to one another.
